title: Flex bundle pricing behind a percentage rollout
name: Flex fare rollout

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code decides which users get the flex_bundle_pricing flag? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: In FlagEvaluator.bucket, a random jitter is added to the hash-derived value. Bucketing is supposed to be deterministic per (flag, user), but with the jitter the same user lands in a different bucket on every call. A user can see flex prices during search and then fail the stillFlex check in confirmOffer ("pricing changed"), and the effective rollout is not sticky, making metrics and support cases inconsistent. The bucket should depend only on the hash.

choiceQuestions.prompt: An operator sets flex_bundle_pricing to enabled with percentage 0 but adds user u-42 to allowUserIds. u-42 searches from a market listed in denyMarkets. What does isEnabled return for u-42?
choices: false, because denyMarkets is checked before percentage
true, because the allow list is checked before the market deny list
It throws because percentage 0 is invalid
choiceQuestions.explanation: isEnabled returns true as soon as allowUserIds includes the user, before denyMarkets or the percentage are looked at. The deny list only applies to users not explicitly allowed, and percentage 0 only affects the bucket comparison, which is never reached. Nothing validates percentage.

choiceQuestions.prompt: An operator flips flex_bundle_pricing from enabled to disabled (via replaceRules) between a user's search and their confirmOffer call. What happens to a user who was shown a flex offer?
choices: They are charged the saved flex total without any check
confirmOffer silently converts the offer to standard pricing
confirmOffer throws "pricing changed" and the user must search again
The saved offers are deleted from the QuoteStore
choiceQuestions.explanation: confirmOffer re-evaluates the flag and compares it to the saved offer's bundle. Saved bundle is flex, stillFlex is now false, so it throws the pricing-changed error. It does not reprice or delete anything, and it does not accept the stale flex offer.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Why does bucket() hash the flag name together with the user ID rather than hashing only the user ID?
choices: So that different flags at the same percentage roll out to different subsets of users
So that the hash is shorter and faster to compute
So that a disabled flag always produces bucket 0
So that the rollout percentage can exceed 100
choiceQuestions.explanation: Including the flag name in the hash input makes each flag's buckets independent; hashing only the user ID would put the same users first in line for every rollout. It has no effect on hash length or speed, disabled flags return before bucket() is called, and the modulo keeps buckets in 0-99 regardless.
